schemes.name: Microfinance Ireland Business Loan
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; eligible microenterprises
schemes.administrator: Microfinance Ireland; referral support through Local Enterprise Offices
schemes.audience: Viable microenterprises unable to obtain sufficient commercial finance
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum loan principal, not a grant or a €50,000 saving. Repayment, interest and credit assessment apply.
schemes.frequency: Business financing; term depends on the loan package
schemes.eligibility: Normally fewer than 10 employees and turnover below €2 million, viable business proposal and insufficient access to commercial borrowing.
schemes.evidenceNote: Current official LEO and government-funded operator pages give the €50,000 maximum; older Localgov summary uses €25,000.
schemes.notes: Business viability/credit assessment is not a household-benefit means test. Do not infer a current APR without checking the selected package.

schemes.name: Arts, Theatre and Dolores O'Riordan Bursaries | Limerick 2026
schemes.area: Limerick City and County; artists based or operating substantially locally
schemes.administrator: Limerick City and County Council Arts Office
schemes.audience: Professional artists, theatre practitioners and musicians
schemes.amountBasis: Theatre maximum €5,000; Individual Arts and Dolores O'Riordan Music maximum €4,000 each. These are separate competitive strands.
schemes.eligibility: Professional-development or new-work proposals. Full-time students and, in this round, film practitioners were excluded.
schemes.evidenceNote: Council page gives each strand's cap and the earlier application deadline.

schemes.name: Burial Ground Maintenance Grants | Limerick
schemes.area: Limerick City and County
schemes.audience: Community burial-ground maintenance committees
schemes.amountBasis: Variable award subject to council budget; no fixed cap published on the inspected page.
schemes.effectivePeriod: Standing scheme; annual forms normally issued in June
schemes.eligibility: Assistance with grass cutting, maintenance and consumables. New committees request an application from the council.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page explains eligible activity and annual application process; exact current deadline requires confirmation.
schemes.notes: Contact published by council: cemeteries@limerick.ie; 061 557015.

schemes.name: Creative Communities Small Grants | Limerick 2026
schemes.area: Limerick City and County
schemes.administrator: Limerick City and County Council / Creative Ireland
schemes.audience: Local community organisations, groups and creatives
schemes.amountBasis: Award cap not verified from the HTML page; linked guidelines require extraction.
schemes.eligibility: Activities taking place in 2026 aligned with Limerick's culture and creativity priorities.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page confirms audience, purpose and closure. Monetary details remain unverified.
schemes.notes: Do not substitute an amount copied from a third-party listing.

schemes.name: Economic and Social Intervention Fund | Limerick 2026
schemes.area: Four Limerick regeneration areas and other qualifying disadvantaged areas in Limerick City
schemes.administrator: Limerick City and County Council / Department of Housing
schemes.audience: Eligible community and social-development projects
schemes.amountBasis: Project award varies. The €1.5 million figure is the 2026 programme allocation, NOT an individual grant.
schemes.eligibility: Projects in qualifying locations addressing the fund's social/economic themes; area selection refers to the 2022 Pobal HP Deprivation Index.
schemes.evidenceNote: Current council page explicitly states the 2026 round is closed.

schemes.name: Going for Gold | Limerick 2026
schemes.area: Limerick City and County
schemes.administrator: Limerick City and County Council and programme partners
schemes.audience: Eligible local communities and competition entrants
schemes.amountBasis: Category-specific grants/prizes; individual 2026 amounts not verified.
schemes.eligibility: Community/environmental improvement programme; categories and entry requirements need separate extraction.
schemes.evidenceNote: Page says 'open' but gives a past 27 March 2026 deadline; date controls this record.
schemes.notes: Do not use previous-year prize-pool headlines as current individual awards. Council-published programme includes non-government partners.

schemes.name: Local Enhancement Programme | Limerick 2026
schemes.area: Limerick City and County
schemes.administrator: Limerick LCDC / Limerick City and County Council
schemes.audience: Not-for-profit community and voluntary groups
schemes.amountBasis: Measure 2 maximum €6,000; Measure 1 up to €1,000. Council-wide allocation is not the applicant award.
schemes.eligibility: Community-use equipment and small capital improvements, with priority for disadvantaged communities; individuals and commercial organisations excluded.
schemes.evidenceNote: Council page gives local award bands, exclusions, supporting documents and the closing date.

schemes.name: Open-Space Maintenance Grant | Limerick housing estates
schemes.area: Limerick City and County; eligible housing developments
schemes.audience: Residents' committees
schemes.amountBasis: Contribution towards grass cutting; award formula not verified from the HTML page.
schemes.effectivePeriod: 2026 documents linked on the official page
schemes.eligibility: Residents' committees maintaining estate open spaces; linked 2026 application and advert contain further requirements.
schemes.evidenceNote: Scheme existence, audience and 2026 forms verified; amount and deadline require document review.

schemes.name: Strategic Fund for Culture and Arts | Limerick 2026
schemes.area: Limerick City and County
schemes.administrator: Limerick City and County Council Arts Office
schemes.audience: Limerick-based creatives and projects securing national/international funding
schemes.amountBasis: 10% support up to €5,000, linked to successful national or international grant funding.
schemes.effectivePeriod: Opportunities through 31 December 2026; subject to remaining budget
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying Limerick creative projects; success in the external funding application and scheme guidelines apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Council states ongoing applications while budget is available; remaining budget not independently confirmed.

schemes.name: Carer's Allowance
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Low-income full-time carers aged 18 or over
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum personal weekly rate for carers aged 66+. Under 66: €270. Half-rate and dependent additions differ.
schemes.effectivePeriod: 2026 personal rates; income disregards require date-specific rules
schemes.eligibility: Full-time care, habitual residence and means conditions; combined work, study, training and voluntary work generally limited to 18.5 hours weekly.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official rate table distinguishes under-66, age-66+, full-rate and half-rate amounts.
schemes.notes: Do not equate income disregards with a simple universal household income ceiling.

schemes.name: Carer's Support Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Qualifying full-time carers
schemes.amountBasis: Annual payment for each qualifying person cared for.
schemes.eligibility: Full-time care and scheme-specific duration/residence conditions apply. Some recipients are paid automatically; other qualifying carers can apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official rate section states €2,000 per care recipient, normally paid in June.

schemes.name: Disability Allowance
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: People aged 16 to under 66 with a qualifying disability
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum weekly personal rate; assessed means can reduce it. Adult/child additions are separate.
schemes.eligibility: Disability expected to last at least one year, substantial restriction on suitable work, means test and habitual residence conditions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official 2026 page sets the personal rate at €254 and describes age, disability and means conditions.

schemes.name: Domiciliary Care Allowance
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Carers of qualifying children under 16 with severe disabilities
schemes.amountBasis: 2026 standard monthly rate; residential-care and other circumstances can affect entitlement.
schemes.eligibility: Child requires ongoing care and attention substantially beyond that normally required by a child of the same age; expected duration and residence/care conditions apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Eligibility checked against January 2026 operational guidelines. €380 rate also confirmed by the department's 2026 annual carers-forum announcement.
schemes.notes: Secondary rate source: https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-social-protection/press-releases/minister-calleary-engages-with-carers-at-annual-forum/ . Do not count an associated Carer's Support Grant twice.

schemes.name: Home Support Service for Older People
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; local HSE needs assessment and delivery
schemes.audience: Normally age 65+; some younger people with qualifying needs
schemes.amountBasis: Free assessed home-support services. Hours and service package vary; no guaranteed national cash value.
schemes.eligibility: Help to remain or return home, based on care needs. A medical card is not required.
schemes.evidenceNote: HSE explicitly states the service is free and income is not checked.
schemes.notes: Consumer Directed Home Support is a delivery option, not a second unrestricted cash entitlement.

schemes.name: Housing Adaptation Grant for Disabled People
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; administered by the applicant's local authority
schemes.administrator: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage / local authorities
schemes.audience: Disabled residents requiring home adaptations; homeowners applying for household members
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum award; up to 100% of approved costs for the lowest income band, tapering for higher incomes.
schemes.eligibility: Necessary disability-related adaptations. Full grant band up to €37,500 gross household income; taper up to €75,000. Local assessment and approval apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Administering department confirms €40,000 and the updated income bands.
schemes.notes: Localgov page mixes €60,000 and €75,000 thresholds. Use the department's current rules and council application form; local funding availability not independently confirmed for all 31 councils.

schemes.name: Mobility Aids Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; local authority of the property
schemes.administrator: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage / local authorities
schemes.audience: People requiring basic adaptations to address mobility needs
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum award; may cover 100% of approved works.
schemes.eligibility: Basic mobility works such as rails, accessible showers or lifts; maximum grant may apply to gross household incomes up to €37,500.
schemes.evidenceNote: Department page confirms €8,000 and the €37,500 household-income threshold.
schemes.notes: Do not use Localgov's older €6,000 / €30,000 figures. Avoid counting this and the larger adaptation grant for the same works without checking overlap rules.

schemes.name: Nursing Homes Support Scheme | Fair Deal
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; approved long-term nursing-home care
schemes.audience: People assessed as needing long-term nursing-home care
schemes.amountBasis: HSE pays the approved balance after an assessed personal contribution. No fixed award; optional nursing-home loan is separate.
schemes.eligibility: Care-needs and financial assessments; approved nursing home. Short-term respite and additional services are not automatically covered.
schemes.evidenceNote: HSE distinguishes care approval, financial assessment and optional loan support.
schemes.notes: Do not model the optional asset-based loan as a free grant.

schemes.name: Seniors Alert Scheme
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; areas served by registered local community organisations
schemes.administrator: Pobal / registered community, voluntary and not-for-profit organisations
schemes.audience: Eligible people aged 65+ of limited means or resources
schemes.amountBasis: Support for a monitored personal alarm; no verified fixed household cash value recorded.
schemes.eligibility: Age 65+, limited means/resources, qualifying living-alone or caring circumstances, local registered-organisation coverage and ability to benefit from the equipment.
schemes.evidenceNote: Pobal page lists participant criteria and the county-searchable registered-organisation directory.
schemes.notes: No numerical income threshold or monitoring-fee duration inferred from the summary page. Apply through a registered organisation.

schemes.name: Back to School Clothing and Footwear Allowance | 2026
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Eligible low-income families with qualifying children
schemes.amountBasis: €285 per eligible child aged 12–22; €160 for ages 2–11. Ages 18–22 require return to full-time second-level education.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying welfare/support route, child and household-income conditions; some families paid automatically.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official 3 June 2026 announcement gives both age bands and the 30 September 2026 closing date.
schemes.notes: Do not present as open on 4 October 2026. No 2027 deadline inferred.

schemes.name: Early Childhood Care and Education Programme | ECCE
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; participating preschool services
schemes.administrator: Department of Children, Disability and Equality / participating providers
schemes.audience: Children in the qualifying preschool age window
schemes.amountBasis: Free preschool provision, normally three hours daily, five days weekly over the programme year; not a household cash award.
schemes.eligibility: Normally at least 2 years 8 months by 31 August and no older than 5 years 6 months by 30 June; participating provider and programme rules apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official programme description gives the preschool hours and age criteria.
schemes.notes: Additional childcare beyond ECCE provision can carry charges; do not also claim NCS for the same ECCE hours.

schemes.name: National Childcare Scheme | Income-assessed subsidy
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; participating registered childcare providers
schemes.administrator: Department of Children, Disability and Equality / Pobal
schemes.audience: Eligible families with children aged 24 weeks to 15 years
schemes.amountBasis: Variable hourly rate determined by income, child age, family size and educational stage.
schemes.eligibility: Reckonable-income ceiling €68,000 from 31 August 2026. Work/study conditions affect maximum hours: 45 or 20 weekly; school/ECCE hours excluded.
schemes.evidenceNote: The official page retains older figures alongside dated 31 August 2026 changes; applicable date matters.
schemes.notes: A fee subsidy, not a fixed cash award. Reckonable income differs from gross salary.

schemes.name: National Childcare Scheme | Universal subsidy
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; participating registered childcare providers
schemes.administrator: Department of Children, Disability and Equality / Pobal
schemes.audience: Families with children aged 24 weeks to 15 years
schemes.amountBasis: €2.14 per eligible childcare hour, up to 45 hours weekly; paid to the provider, not as household cash.
schemes.eligibility: Eligible child and participating provider; school/ECCE hours excluded.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official NCS subsidy guidance.
schemes.notes: Alternative to the income-assessed rate, not a second payment for the same childcare hour.

schemes.name: SUSI Post-Leaving Certificate Maintenance Grant | 2026/27
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; approved PLC courses
schemes.audience: Eligible students on approved PLC courses
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum annual special non-adjacent rate; adjacent special rate €3,230. Ordinary and partial rates are lower.
schemes.eligibility: Approved course, residence, nationality, progression and means requirements; distance and special-rate conditions apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official PLC income thresholds and maintenance-rate table.
schemes.notes: A course-specific variant, not an additional maintenance award to add to undergraduate funding.

schemes.name: SUSI Postgraduate Fee Grant | 2026/27
schemes.area: Approved postgraduate courses within the State
schemes.audience: Eligible postgraduate students
schemes.amountBasis: Special-rate tuition support up to €6,270. Standard postgraduate fee contribution up to €4,500; separate maintenance conditions apply.
schemes.frequency: Academic year; fee support paid to institution
schemes.eligibility: Approved course, nationality, residence, progression and household-income conditions; special rate requires additional qualifying conditions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official postgraduate table distinguishes special fee support from ordinary fee contribution and maintenance.

schemes.name: SUSI Undergraduate Maintenance Grant | 2026/27
schemes.area: Eligible students on approved courses within the State
schemes.audience: Eligible undergraduate students
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum annual special non-adjacent maintenance rate. Ordinary full non-adjacent rate €4,722; lower/adjacent bands differ. Fees are separate.
schemes.eligibility: Means, nationality, residence, progression and approved-course rules; distance and special-rate welfare conditions affect amount. BTEA recipients cannot also receive maintenance.
schemes.evidenceNote: 2026/27 rate table; special-rate and distance criteria apply.

schemes.name: Domestic Waste Water Treatment System Grant | inspection route
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; qualifying local-authority inspection cases
schemes.audience: Homeowners with a qualifying defective septic-tank system
schemes.amountBasis: 85% of eligible remedial costs up to €12,000; paid after satisfactory completion.
schemes.eligibility: Council notification of an inspection fault, permanently occupied home and seven-year conditions; routine servicing and desludging excluded.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page confirms the 85% rate and €12,000 cap for the described inspection route.
schemes.notes: Other water-quality priority-area routes require separate eligibility records; not every septic-tank owner qualifies.

schemes.name: Energy-Efficient Windows and External Doors Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Owners of qualifying pre-2011 properties
schemes.amountBasis: Windows cap: €4,000 detached, €3,000 semi/end-terrace, €1,800 mid-terrace, €1,500 apartment. Doors are separately €800 each, maximum two.
schemes.eligibility: Good attic/wall insulation or qualifying heat-loss result, specified product standards, ventilation and post-works BER; grant approval before works.
schemes.evidenceNote: SEAI permits windows, doors or both; the numeric field stores the highest windows cap, not a combined guaranteed award.

schemes.name: Enhanced Solar PV and Battery Support | qualifying welfare recipients
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; separate RAS Dublin pilot must not be generalised
schemes.audience: Eligible homeowners receiving specified DSP payments
schemes.amountBasis: Announced maximum for solar PV and battery support; final terms and opening require confirmation.
schemes.eligibility: Specified welfare-payment routes; some require duration, child-age or co-residence conditions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official announcement, not a completed operational eligibility specification.
schemes.notes: FUTURE / NOT LIVE VERIFIED on 4 October. The separate Dublin RAS pilot is not nationwide renter eligibility.

schemes.name: Fuel Allowance
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; one award per qualifying household
schemes.audience: Eligible older people and qualifying welfare recipients
schemes.amountBasis: Weekly seasonal rate, not a year-round weekly payment. Season length and exceptional extensions must be checked.
schemes.frequency: Weekly during fuel season; instalment options on some schemes
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying age/payment, household composition and means rules. Working Family Payment became a qualifying route in 2026.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page states €38 weekly and separately explains the 2026 extension and WFP route.
schemes.notes: Do not automatically multiply by 52 or carry the exceptional 2025/26 extension into later seasons.

schemes.name: Heat Pump System Grant | three-component bundle
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Owners of qualifying homes changing heating systems
schemes.amountBasis: House bundle maximum: €6,500 unit, €2,000 eligible distribution upgrades and €4,000 renewable-heat bonus. Apartment/air-to-air/replacement-system caps differ.
schemes.effectivePeriod: Bundle introduced February 2026; September scrappage announcement is separate
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying property and heat-loss standard; technical assessment or permitted declaration; individual component eligibility must be established.
schemes.evidenceNote: SEAI gives bundle components, dwelling-specific amounts and heat-loss rules.
schemes.notes: €12,500 is not payable for every installation. Avoid adding component amounts again to the bundle total.

schemes.name: Home Battery Grant | announced October 2026
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; detailed eligibility pending
schemes.audience: Eligible households under forthcoming implementation rules
schemes.amountBasis: Announced battery-support amount; not confirmed as claimable on research date.
schemes.effectivePeriod: Announced opening 2026-10-06, subject to final implementation
schemes.eligibility: Full implementation terms were not yet published in the inspected announcement.
schemes.evidenceNote: 29 September SEAI announcement; future opening date.
schemes.notes: FUTURE / NOT LIVE VERIFIED. Do not treat as currently available or use predicted energy savings as grant value.

schemes.name: Household Benefits Package
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; one package per household
schemes.audience: People aged 70+ and eligible younger pensioners, disabled people and carers
schemes.amountBasis: Electricity OR gas allowance per day, paid monthly; free TV licence is a separate in-kind component.
schemes.eligibility: Full-time residence and one package per household. No means test at age 70+; younger applicants have qualifying-payment or other conditions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Current official page gives €1.15 per day, rather than a fixed €35 monthly amount.
schemes.notes: Do not count separate electricity and gas allowances for the same household.

schemes.name: Private Well Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; homes relying on eligible private water supplies
schemes.audience: Eligible homeowners with deficient private water supplies
schemes.amountBasis: New well: 85% of approved costs up to €5,000; rehabilitation: 85% up to €3,000; treatment: 100% up to €1,000.
schemes.eligibility: Normal residence, inadequate quality/quantity, inability to connect to public/group supply and seven-year home/prior-grant conditions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page gives separate new-well, rehabilitation and treatment rates, plus a €750 minimum threshold.
schemes.notes: €5,000 is the new-well component cap, not a verified cap for every possible combination of works.

schemes.name: Solar Electricity PV Grant | standard route
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Eligible homeowners and other qualifying property owners
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum standard installation grant, determined by system capacity.
schemes.effectivePeriod: Standard 2026 rate; future eligibility change separately flagged
schemes.eligibility: MPRN, qualifying property age, approved installation and prior-funding rules. The existing page uses pre-2021 occupation; announced pre-2025 expansion starts 6 October 2026.
schemes.evidenceNote: Standard grant page checked; 29 September announcement requires date-sensitive eligibility versioning.
schemes.notes: Do not apply future 6 October conditions on 4 October. Enhanced welfare-linked solar/battery route is distinct.

schemes.name: Warmer Homes Scheme | fully funded energy upgrades
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; qualifying owner-occupied homes
schemes.audience: Eligible homeowners receiving specified social-protection payments
schemes.amountBasis: Approved energy upgrades fully funded following assessment; no fixed personal cash award.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying ownership, home and welfare-payment conditions. Measures depend on the home assessment and programme rules.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official fully funded programme page; do not substitute optional individual-insulation grant values as the scheme's total value.
schemes.notes: Solar/battery expansion announced for 6 October 2026 is not treated as already implemented.

schemes.name: Drugs Payment Scheme
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Residents and qualifying family members
schemes.amountBasis: €80 maximum household spend per calendar month on approved prescribed medicines and specified equipment rental. €80 is a cost cap, NOT a grant.
schemes.eligibility: Living in Ireland and intending to remain at least one year; family/dependant rules apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: HSE specifies the €80 household cap and no means test.
schemes.notes: Cash amount left blank deliberately. Refunds relate to eligible expenditure above the cap, not all pharmacy purchases.

schemes.name: GP Visit Card | carers
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Recipients of Carer's Allowance or Carer's Benefit
schemes.amountBasis: Covered GP visits; not a cash award.
schemes.eligibility: Full-rate and half-rate recipients of either qualifying carer payment can register.
schemes.evidenceNote: Eligibility derives from the qualifying carer payment, not a new general GP-card means calculation.

schemes.name: GP Visit Card | children under 8
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Children under 8
schemes.amountBasis: Covered GP visits; no fixed monetary benefit.
schemes.eligibility: Parent or guardian registers an eligible child; medicines are not automatically included.
schemes.evidenceNote: HSE lists a separate under-8 registration route.

schemes.name: GP Visit Card | general age 8–69
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Residents aged 8–69 meeting the assessment
schemes.amountBasis: Covered GP visits; not a cash payment or full medical card.
schemes.eligibility: General income-and-expenses assessment. Medicines and other services are not automatically covered.
schemes.evidenceNote: HSE general-card route is distinct from age-based and carer registration.

schemes.name: GP Visit Card | over-70s route
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Residents qualifying for the HSE over-70s card
schemes.amountBasis: Covered GP visits, not medicines or a cash award.
schemes.eligibility: Age-based registration; check the dedicated HSE page for residence requirements.
schemes.evidenceNote: Dedicated HSE age-based card guidance.

schemes.name: Long-Term Illness Scheme
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: People with one of the specified qualifying conditions
schemes.amountBasis: Approved medicines and appliances for the qualifying condition, not a fixed payment.
schemes.eligibility: Residence and a listed condition, with medical certification. Coverage is condition-specific, not all prescriptions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official HSE scheme description and linked application route.

schemes.name: Medical Card
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Eligible residents; financial and automatic-qualification routes
schemes.amountBasis: Healthcare coverage, not a fixed cash award. Covers GP care and specified other services; some prescription charges can remain.
schemes.eligibility: Ordinary residence and financial assessment normally apply, with automatic and discretionary routes for specified circumstances.
schemes.evidenceNote: HSE coverage and application guidance; actual entitlement depends on the qualifying route.

schemes.name: Domestic Lead Remediation Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; local authority of the home
schemes.audience: Eligible owner-occupiers and long-term tenants replacing domestic lead drinking-water pipes
schemes.amountBasis: 100% of eligible costs up to €5,000 per home.
schemes.eligibility: Normal residence; tenants need owner permission. Holiday homes and specified public/institutional housing are excluded.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official local-government scheme page describes the €5,000 cap and absence of a means test.
schemes.notes: Confirm current claim form and documentation with the council before application.

schemes.name: Help to Buy Scheme
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; qualifying new-build or self-build home
schemes.audience: Qualifying first-time buyers
schemes.amountBasis: Per-property maximum: lowest of €30,000, 10% of eligible value, and qualifying Income Tax/DIRT paid in the four preceding application years.
schemes.eligibility: First-time purchase, eligible property up to €500,000, qualifying finance normally at least 70%, tax compliance and five-year main-residence requirement.
schemes.evidenceNote: Revenue confirms the three-way cap and per-property rather than per-buyer limit.
schemes.notes: USC and PRSI do not count towards the refund; clawback conditions apply.

schemes.name: Housing Aid for Older People Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; local authority of the property
schemes.administrator: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage / local authorities
schemes.audience: Normally people aged 66+ living in poor housing conditions
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum award; up to 100% of approved works in the lowest income band, tapering with income.
schemes.eligibility: Essential repairs to support remaining at home; normally age 66+, with hardship exceptions. Income bands up to €75,000; written approval before work.
schemes.evidenceNote: Department page gives €10,700, income bands and eligible-work restrictions.
schemes.notes: Localgov's older €8,000 entry is outdated. Council-specific budget availability and technical documents must be checked.

schemes.name: Housing Assistance Payment | HAP
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; applicant's local authority and household-size rent limits
schemes.audience: Households qualified for social housing support
schemes.amountBasis: Variable council payment to the landlord, subject to applicable rent limits and assessment. Tenant contributions are separate; no single national grant amount.
schemes.eligibility: Local-authority social-housing qualification, eligible accommodation and landlord/tenancy requirements.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official HAP portal confirms council-administered support, social-housing qualification and monthly landlord payment.
schemes.notes: Council rent limits, discretionary uplifts and homeless-HAP variants need their own records before calculating eligibility or award.

schemes.name: Repair and Leasing Scheme
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; property must meet local social-housing demand
schemes.administrator: Local authorities and approved housing bodies
schemes.audience: Owners or purchasers of eligible vacant properties
schemes.amountBasis: Interest-free loan principal up to €80,000 including VAT per home; repayable through lease deductions.
schemes.eligibility: Property normally vacant at least 12 months, suitable for social housing, with council assessment and tax compliance. Financing-need exceptions apply to some commercial conversions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Department guidance gives €80,000 per home; Localgov's €60,000 entry is older.
schemes.notes: Not a free grant or €80,000 saving. Approval depends on property suitability and local demand.

schemes.name: Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; island variants require separate checking
schemes.administrator: Local authorities / Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
schemes.audience: Owners refurbishing an eligible vacant property for residence or rental
schemes.amountBasis: Standard base grant up to €50,000; qualifying derelict-property top-up €20,000. €70,000 is not the base award.
schemes.eligibility: Standard published criteria include vacancy for at least two years and construction up to 2007; prior council approval, occupation/rental and clawback conditions apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official local-government page distinguishes the €50,000 base and €20,000 dereliction top-up.
schemes.notes: Record island uplifts and any later expansions as separate rule variants; do not infer them from this standard record.

schemes.name: Additional Needs Payment
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; local Community Welfare Service assessment
schemes.administrator: Department of Social Protection / Community Welfare Service
schemes.audience: Households unable to meet essential exceptional expenditure
schemes.amountBasis: Discretionary assessed assistance; no fixed national payment rate.
schemes.frequency: As assessed for the qualifying need
schemes.eligibility: Household income, expenses, resources and the essential need are assessed. Published income guidelines do not remove officer discretion.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page explicitly says there is no set rate of payment.
schemes.notes: Income guideline amounts are not benefit values.

schemes.name: Adoptive Benefit
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Qualifying employed or self-employed adopting parents
schemes.amountBasis: Standard weekly amount for 24 weeks; dependent comparison rules may apply.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying adoptive leave, sufficient PRSI and adoption certification. Late leave commencement can reduce the payable period.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official service page specifies €299 for 24 weeks.

schemes.name: Child Benefit
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; cross-border coordination rules may apply
schemes.audience: Parents and guardians of qualifying children
schemes.amountBasis: Standard monthly amount per child. Twins: €210 each; other multiple births: €280 each.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying child and claimant residence/care conditions apply. Check age, education and cross-border rules on the linked page.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official Rates of payment section gives €140 standard rate and separate multiple-birth rates.

schemes.name: Jobseeker's Allowance
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Qualifying jobseekers with limited means
schemes.amountBasis: 2026 maximum weekly personal rate for age 25+. Standard age 18–24 rate is €163.70, with exceptions allowing the full rate.
schemes.eligibility: Means and habitual-residence conditions, capable of and available for work, genuinely seeking work; unemployment-day rules and self-employment exceptions apply.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official February 2026 service guidance includes age bands and qualification rules.
schemes.notes: Not the same scheme as contribution-based or pay-related jobseeker benefits.

schemes.name: Living Alone Increase
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: People living alone who receive a qualifying pension or disability payment
schemes.amountBasis: Additional weekly amount attached to a qualifying main payment.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying main payment and living-alone conditions, including specific exceptions for independent accommodation and overnight security support.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official rate section gives €22; qualifying-payment and living-alone rules remain essential.
schemes.notes: Means-test classification reflects dependence on the underlying payment; no separate universal income rule should be inferred.

schemes.name: Maternity Benefit
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; social insurance coordination may apply
schemes.audience: Eligible employed and self-employed people on maternity leave
schemes.amountBasis: Standard weekly rate for 26 weeks; half-rate, dependent comparison and premature-birth exceptions apply.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying maternity leave and sufficient PRSI contributions, with medical and employment certification.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official service page states €299 weekly for 26 weeks.
schemes.notes: Taxable benefit. Employer salary continuation does not automatically create additional take-home income.

schemes.name: Newborn Baby Grant
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Families with a qualifying newborn child
schemes.amountBasis: Additional once-off payment, separate from the first monthly Child Benefit payment.
schemes.eligibility: Paid with Child Benefit for children born on or after 1 December 2024, subject to Child Benefit conditions.
schemes.evidenceNote: Child Benefit page explicitly records the additional €280 newborn payment.
schemes.notes: Do not count the first €140 Child Benefit payment twice.

schemes.name: Parent's Benefit
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Eligible employed and self-employed parents taking parent's leave
schemes.amountBasis: Standard weekly amount; nine weeks per qualifying parent.
schemes.frequency: Weekly blocks; up to nine weeks
schemes.eligibility: Sufficient PRSI; qualifying parent's leave within two years of birth or adoption placement; apply within six months of taking leave.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official service page distinguishes nine weeks per parent from maternity and paternity entitlements.

schemes.name: Paternity Benefit
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Eligible employed and self-employed parents on paternity leave
schemes.amountBasis: Standard weekly rate for two consecutive weeks; exceptions apply.
schemes.eligibility: Sufficient PRSI and certified paternity leave; leave must start within 26 weeks of birth or adoption.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official page records the €299 rate, consecutive-week rule and leave window.
schemes.notes: Taxable. Relative claim deadlines must be calculated from the person's dates, not stored as one national date.

schemes.name: State Pension | Contributory
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; contribution and international coordination rules vary
schemes.audience: People aged 66+ with sufficient qualifying social-insurance contributions
schemes.amountBasis: 2026 maximum standard weekly personal rate at age 66, before age-80 additions or qualifying deferral uplifts. Actual rate depends on contribution record.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying PRSI record and pension age. Caring credits, overseas contributions and optional later drawdown can affect entitlement.
schemes.evidenceNote: Department service page gives the standard 2026 rate and contribution-based qualification. Adult additions can have a separate means test.
schemes.notes: Taxable. Do not describe €299.30 as the maximum across every age and deferral scenario.

schemes.name: State Pension | Non-contributory
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland
schemes.audience: Eligible residents aged 66+ without an adequate contributory pension
schemes.amountBasis: 2026 maximum weekly personal rate at age 80+. Maximum for ages 66–79 is €288; means can reduce the award.
schemes.eligibility: Age, habitual residence and assessed means conditions; considered as an alternative to a contributory pension, not an additional full pension.
schemes.evidenceNote: Department service page distinguishes the age-based personal rates and means assessment.

schemes.name: Working Family Payment
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; EU coordination exceptions may apply
schemes.audience: Employees with dependent children and low family income
schemes.amountBasis: 60% of the difference between assessed weekly family income and the applicable family-size income limit; not a fixed grant.
schemes.eligibility: Employment and dependent-child conditions apply. 2026 weekly family-income limits start at €765 for one child and €866 for two; these are eligibility limits, not awards.
schemes.evidenceNote: Official rate section specifies the 60% formula and family-size income limits.
schemes.notes: Retain all income deductions and family-size bands before implementing an eligibility calculator.

schemes.name: Health Expenses Tax Relief
schemes.area: Ireland income-tax system; qualifying expenses may be incurred elsewhere
schemes.audience: Taxpayers who paid eligible unreimbursed health expenses
schemes.amountBasis: Generally 20% of eligible unreimbursed costs. Qualifying nursing-home expenses can receive relief at the claimant's higher tax rate.
schemes.eligibility: Claimant must have paid the cost; insurance, HSE or other reimbursements must be deducted. Only qualifying treatments/expenses.
schemes.evidenceNote: Revenue identifies 20% general relief, nursing-home exception and four-year refund rule.
schemes.notes: 20 is a percentage, not a €20 benefit; numeric amount deliberately blank.

schemes.name: Home Carer Tax Credit
schemes.area: Ireland income-tax system
schemes.audience: Jointly assessed married couples/civil partners with a qualifying home carer
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum 2026 annual credit; reduced above €7,200 carer income and unavailable at €11,100 or more.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying dependent person, joint assessment and carer-income rules. DSP Carer's Allowance/Benefit is excluded from this income test.
schemes.evidenceNote: Revenue rates and qualification pages checked.
schemes.notes: Cannot be combined with the increased standard-rate band for dual-income couples; compare the alternatives.

schemes.name: Rent Tax Credit
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; qualifying rental arrangements
schemes.audience: Taxpayers paying qualifying rent
schemes.amountBasis: Maximum annual credit for a jointly assessed couple; €1,000 for an individual. Limited by qualifying rent and income-tax liability.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying tenancy/rent, landlord relationship and tax-liability rules; social-housing support exclusions must be checked.
schemes.evidenceNote: Revenue overview and in-year/prior-year claim guidance; household and individual caps differ.
schemes.notes: Not an automatic refundable payment of €2,000. Review each prior tax year separately.

schemes.name: Free Travel Scheme
schemes.area: Republic of Ireland; participating services and cross-border arrangements differ
schemes.administrator: Department of Social Protection / participating transport operators
schemes.audience: Qualifying residents aged 66+ and specified younger disability/carer groups
schemes.amountBasis: Travel concession on participating services; no fixed cash payment or universal annual saving.
schemes.frequency: While eligible and pass is valid
schemes.effectivePeriod: Operational rules checked March 2026; paper-pass change from 2026-03-01
schemes.eligibility: Age/residence or a qualifying younger-person route. A valid, in-date Free Travel Public Services Card is required; paper passes ceased to be valid from 1 March 2026.
schemes.evidenceNote: Department service page covers age and qualifying-payment routes, pass requirements and service restrictions.
schemes.notes: No separate means test for the age-based route; some younger routes depend on a qualifying payment. Northern Ireland internal travel can require a separate Senior SmartPass.
